{{Quote|First and foremost, Xim, Son of Xer, you are charged with causing the extermination and extinction of nine sentient species.''"<br />"''Nine? I know I spaced more than that.''"<br />"''Among them the Qadel, the Ermi, the Veeza, and the Zoa'mon&hellip;''"<br />"''Slavers all. I did the galaxy a favor.|Rexrax Shool accuses Xim during his trial in the play ''Evocar''|<ref name="Xim Week 4" />}}
The '''Veeza''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. According to the play [[Evocar (play)|''Evocar'']], which was written by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Author/Legends|playwright]] [[Direus'pei]]<ref name="Xim Week 4" /> between [[920 BBY]] and [[671 BBY]],<ref name="Evocar date">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek05/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part IV: ''Evocar'')|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}} dates [[Direus'pei]] [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] to [[920 BBY]] and [[Death/Legends|death]] to [[671 BBY]], thus the play [[Evocar (play)|''Evocar'']] must have been written between those dates.</ref> the Veeza were exterminated by the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] during his [[Xim's Expansionist Period|conquests]]<ref name="Xim Week 4" /> of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] that occurred between [[25,130 BBY|25,130]] and [[25,100 BBY]].<ref name="The History of Xim">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-extra-the-history-of-xim-and-the-tion-cluster|text=Essential Atlas Extra: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}} dates the end of [[Xim/Legends|Xim]]'s predecessor [[Xer VIII]] to [[25,130 BBY]] and the end of Xim's reign to [[25,100 BBY]].</ref> In the play, when Xim was captured and placed on trial by the [[Hutt Empire]], he justified the extinction of the Veeza and other species on the basis that they were [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]].<ref name="Xim Week 4" /> 

However ''[[The Despotica]]'', a collection of literary works about Xim and his conquests, stated that Direus'pei disregarded accepted history while writing the play. It went on to state that the Hutt playright used Xim and other famous figures in ''Evocar'' as a political screed to condemn the Hutts' continued subjugation of the [[Evocii]], a species [[Homeworld/Legends|native]]<ref name="Xim Week 4" /> to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Lords of Nal Hutta">''[[Lords of Nal Hutta]]''</ref> [[Nal Hutta]].<ref name="Xim Week 4" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Veeza were mentioned in the fourth part of [[Michael Kogge]]'s article series ''[[Xim Week: The Despotica]]'', which was published as an exclusive article on [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|''Hyperspace'']] on [[December 11]], [[2009]].<ref name="Xim Week 4" />
